items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: Ross Tompkins and Russell George said, “look I don’t care if he can read a note or not, he swings like crazy and we can teach him to read.” And sure enough, I got hired for the gig

ctx.x: Billy Butterfield and Kai Winding. You got into that?

Yeah. Butterfield came first. I was actually, I had just gotten out of the Navy and actually, no they were sort of interspersed with each other I think, I take that back. I was just about to get discharged from the Navy when my brother and this funky girl that he was dating at the time came down to my house at the Brooklyn Navy Yard and they were all discussing what I was going to do when I got out of the Navy. And I said, “well I could call up Kai Winding and get a job right away.” So she says, “go ahead, do…

going to do with him?” And Ross Tompkins and Russell George said, “look I don’t care if he can read a note or not, he swings like crazy and we can teach him to read.” And sure enough, I got hired for the gig and lo and behold a bit at a time I did learn to read music, as we recently found out. And that sort of led to it all.
